metrics.primary: recall@4 = (number of the question's 2 gold paragraphs that appear in the returned top-4) / 2, averaged over questions, in percent. Identical definition to router_gate_results.json.
metrics.secondary_ann: exact-top-4 agreement = |returned top-4 INTERSECT exhaustive top-4| / 4. This is the metric on VAL-1190 (no gold) and the exactness metric for the screening arms.
metrics.cost_metric_routing: scanned_frac = candidate rows scored exactly / n_docs. EQUAL COST means matched scanned_frac; every table prints the achieved scanned_frac of both arms.
metrics.cost_metric_latency: per-query wall p50 over interleaved replicates, plus resident bytes of the auxiliary structure (centroids + assignment map + screening matrix).

seeds.note: 3 seeds for every arm whose result depends on a k-means fit or a random projection. Bootstrap seed 3, fixed.
seeds.power_caveat: 3 seeds bounds SEED variance; the 95% CI below is over QUESTIONS (n=1000), which is the axis the decision rule names. Seed spread is reported separately and a mechanism whose seed spread exceeds its question CI is called unstable, not a win.

decision_rule_BINDING.statistic: paired bootstrap over questions, 10000 resamples, seed 3, of (arm recall@4 - baseline recall@4) in percentage points, at EQUAL COST as defined above
decision_rule_BINDING.anything_else: NEGATIVE RESULT. Reported with its measured value, never rounded in favour.
decision_rule_BINDING.latency_arms_extra_condition: a mechanism sold on latency or RSS must ALSO show a measured p50 speedup (or resident-byte reduction) over B1 on the same box in interleaved replicates; a recall tie with no cost saving is a negative result.
decision_rule_BINDING.exactness_arms: an arm claiming EXACT top-4 must show 0 differing top-4 sets over all queries AND carry a deterministic certificate (a per-document upper bound that is provably never exceeded), not merely an empirical count.

declared_arms.a_power_mean_pooling: Generalised power mean over page landmarks, p in {-inf(min), -8, -4, -2, -1, -0.5, 0(geometric), 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, +inf(max)}, at matched beam. Baseline B3 (p=max). Also: does argmax_p track a corpus statistic across corpora/layouts?
declared_arms.b_quasirandom_seeding: k-means centroid init by low-discrepancy sequence instead of k-means++. Arms: kmeans++ (B2 init), i.i.d. uniform rows, Halton in the top-m PCA subspace snapped to nearest row, golden-ratio additive recurrence (Kronecker R_d) likewise, and a 1-D projection-quantile variant. Equal Lloyd iterations (10). Judged on (i) downstream recall@4 at matched scanned_frac, (ii) k-means objective, (iii) cell-size imbalance.
declared_arms.c_structured_random_projection: Screen candidates in d' << 768 then re-rank survivors in fp32. Projections: SRHT (Hadamard, matrix-free, O(d log d)), random orthonormal (Gaussian+QR), PCA. KEY: a subsampled Hadamard row set is ORTHONORMAL, so the residual norm is exactly computable and Cauchy-Schwarz gives a DETERMINISTIC per-document upper bound -> certified-exact top-4. Measure (i) empirical pool size for zero top-4 change, (ii) certified survivor count, (iii) latency and resident bytes vs B1.
declared_arms.d_crt_modular_sharding: CRT over coprime moduli. d1: cell derived from the document id alone (zero stored assignment map) -- content-blind. d2: product/multi-index quantiser, J sub-quantisers with PRIME codebook sizes, composite cell recovered by CRT from the residue tuple. Measure map+centroid bytes saved and recall at matched scanned_frac vs B2.
declared_arms.e_tropical_max_plus: Routing aggregation as min-plus in ANGULAR space: page/cell score = min_j (theta(q, c_j) - r_j), r_j = angular radius of landmark j's members. TESTABLE CLAIM over plain max-pooling: cos(theta - r) is an ADMISSIBLE upper bound on any member's cosine, so (i) it should rank cells better than the radius-blind max, and (ii) it certifies a beam -- prune any cell whose bound is below the current 4th-best exact score and the top-4 is provably unchanged.

verdict_ranked.how_to_read: Every number below is a key in this same file. The decision rule is the pre-registered one: paired bootstrap over questions, 10000 resamples, seed 3, at EQUAL COST. CI lower bound > 0 = win, >= +1.0 pt = ship as default, anything else = NEGATIVE RESULT. Under that rule as written this study has ZERO wins and eight negatives: see amendment_2026_09_16_verifier.reclassification.

harness_validation.reading: the harness reproduces the shipped build's own published baseline to the digit on recall and to 0.05 pt on the router, so the deltas below are measuring the mechanisms and not the harness.

ranked_verdict.arm: (c) PCA-256 orthonormal screen + Cauchy-Schwarz residual bound
ranked_verdict.status: NOT A WIN UNDER THE PRE-REGISTERED RULE -- the rule says win = 95% CI lower bound > 0 on a paired-bootstrap RECALL delta, and this arm's recall delta is identically 0, CI [0.00, 0.00]. It satisfies the exactness_arms clause and the latency clause and nothing else. Reported as a real mechanism with no pre-registered category, NOT as a win.
ranked_verdict.what_it_is: project the corpus onto the top-256 eigenvectors of its own Gram matrix, store one extra float per document (the residual norm), screen in 256-d, take a 128-document seed pool, exact-score it to get tau = the 4th-best cosine, then exact-score every document whose upper bound (Pq).(Px) + ||q_res||*||x_res|| >= tau.
ranked_verdict.recall_effect: ZERO by proof, not by measurement: 0 bound violations in 14,286,600 document checks and 0 of 1000 queries with a different top-4 SCORE vector (certificate_audit). Recall CI is exactly [0.00, 0.00].

build_cost.note: the basis is 786 KB and persistable in a container header; the router's 2858 centroids are 8.78 MB and are not, which is why every vault open re-fits them today (DECISIONS #3).

ranked_verdict.why_the_recall_CI_cannot_be_positive: an exactness-preserving mechanism has a recall delta of identically 0, so 'CI lower bound > 0' is unreachable by construction. The pre-registered clause that applies is latency_arms_extra_condition: no recall loss plus a measured p50 saving. Both hold. Reported this way rather than quietly reinterpreting the bar.
ranked_verdict.recommendation: ship as an option behind a flag; make it the default only after an end-to-end engine measurement, because the 1.529x here is an arena-level microbenchmark on 200 queries x 5 interleaved replicates at load average 3.3, and the shipped router already died at exactly this step (arena-level promise, engine-level regression).
ranked_verdict.status_as_published: WIN -- the only arm that clears its bar

ranked_verdict.arm: (c) certificate correctness result, independent of speed
ranked_verdict.status: NOT A WIN UNDER THE PRE-REGISTERED RULE -- a correctness property, which the rule does not score at all.
ranked_verdict.finding: the bound is admissible for ANY orthonormal basis, so its CORRECTNESS does not depend on the basis fitting the data -- a stale PCA basis after appends makes the screen slower (more survivors) and never wrong. Measured: 0 violations for pca d=128, pca d=256 and srht d=256 over 14,286,600 checks each.

ranked_verdict.arm: (a) power-mean pooling over landmarks, p sweep min..max
ranked_verdict.status: NEGATIVE -- max-pooling is at or above the optimum everywhere that matters
ranked_verdict.best_case: TRAIN-71k reclustered, 25% budget: p=64 scores 77.05 against max 77.00, delta +0.05 pt, 95% CI lower bound +0.00. On the random (un-reclustered) layout the best p is 32 with +0.50 / +0.55 / +0.30 pt over three seeds and CI lower bounds -0.25 / -0.15 / -0.45. Nothing clears 0, let alone +1.0.
ranked_verdict.shape_of_the_curve: monotone increasing in p over the whole range: at 71k/25% budget, seed 0, the sweep runs min 52.40, p=1 72.55, p=4 74.75, p=8 76.35, p=32 77.00, p=64 77.05, max 77.00. Every p at or below 4 is a LOSS of between 2.25 pt (p=4) and 24.60 pt (min). The arithmetic mean (p=1) costs 4.45 pt.

predictability_sub_question.reading: the optimum does drift down as pages get less coherent (higher landmark dispersion -> lower best p), which is the mechanism you would predict: max is a single-landmark estimate and a finite p denoises it. But the whole effect lives inside the noise band, so there is nothing to predict that would change a decision.

ranked_verdict.arm: (b) low-discrepancy centroid seeding (Halton over prime bases, Kronecker golden-ratio lattice, van der Corput on the 1st PC)
ranked_verdict.status: NEGATIVE -- and it makes the fit measurably worse by its own objective
ranked_verdict.recall_effect: 24 (init x seed x budget) cells tested against k-means++ at the same seed. 3 cells came back with a CI lower bound above 0 (uniform s2 b0.25 +0.20, kronecker s2 b0.25 +0.40, vdc s1 b0.15 +0.35); none replicates across seeds, all are under +0.5 pt, and 3 positives out of 24 two-sided tests at 95% is the multiplicity artifact you should expect. Plain i.i.d. uniform seeding scores +0.100 pooled, which is the same story without any low-discrepancy mathematics in it.
ranked_verdict.why_it_fails: a low-discrepancy sequence covers a BOX. These vectors occupy a thin curved manifold in 768 dimensions, and the box->data map (rank-uniformise the top-8 principal coordinates, then snap to the nearest data row) is where the discrepancy guarantee is spent. The measured consequence is the balance column: LDS seeds produce cells 30% more unequal in size than k-means++ (0.971 against 0.746, mean of 3 seeds) and a largest cell of 257 rows against 160.

ranked_verdict.arm: (c) STRUCTURED projection specifically (SRHT / Hadamard) and random orthonormal projection
ranked_verdict.status: NEGATIVE -- the structure is not what makes the screen work
ranked_verdict.finding: with a certificate, SRHT-256 and random-ortho-256 must scan 99.9% and 98.8% of the corpus (certified survivors), because a random subspace captures only d/D of the energy: measured captured energy 0.266 (srht-256), 0.350 (ortho-256), 0.934 (pca-256). Certified latency 7.586 ms (srht) and 7.511 ms (ortho) against 1.470 ms exact -- 0.194x and 0.196x, i.e. five times SLOWER.
ranked_verdict.secondary: SRHT pays an extra 1024/768 = 1.33x energy penalty purely from zero-padding 768 up to the next power of two, which is visible as 0.266 against ortho's 0.350.
ranked_verdict.without_a_certificate: srht-256 still needs a pool of 2,230-4,100 documents (3.1-5.7% of 71,433) for zero top-4 change over 1000 queries, against 520 (0.73%) for pca-256. The O(d log d) transform is irrelevant either way: at D=768 both projections cost microseconds and the screening matmul dominates.

ranked_verdict.arm: (e) tropical / min-plus routing with angular radii
ranked_verdict.status: NEGATIVE -- the bound is admissible and useless
ranked_verdict.admissibility: verified: 0 violations in 571,600 (query, cell) checks; the largest true-minus-bound excess is 5.36e-07, about 9 float32 ulps at that cosine, i.e. rounding in arccos/cos and not a failure of the spherical triangle inequality.
ranked_verdict.ranking_effect: LOSS at every budget: -3.12 pt CI[-3.70,-2.55] at 5% budget, -1.13 CI[-1.48,-0.80] at 15%, -0.48 CI[-0.72,-0.25] at 25% (pooled over 3 seeds, 71k). On the page-landmark table it is worse: -13.55 pt at a 5% budget.
ranked_verdict.certified_beam_effect: 99.94% of the corpus must be scanned for a provably exact top-4 -- the bound prunes 0.06%. Mechanism: the mean cell angular radius is 38.9 degrees at cell_target=25, so cos(theta - r) is close to 1 for nearly every cell and the ordering information is destroyed rather than corrected.
ranked_verdict.what_it_buys_over_max_pooling: nothing measurable here. The testable claim was that radius-awareness orders cells better than the radius-blind max; it orders them worse, because subtracting a large radius compresses the score range.
ranked_verdict.contrast_that_explains_arm_1: the same Cauchy-Schwarz/triangle-inequality idea prunes 99.66% of the corpus when the 'radius' is a residual NORM in an energy-compacting basis (arm 1) and 0.06% when it is an angular radius around a k-means centroid. The geometry of the summary, not the algebra of the bound, is what decides.

ranked_verdict.arm: (d) CRT product quantiser with prime codebook sizes
ranked_verdict.status: NEGATIVE on quality, real but small on memory
ranked_verdict.recall_effect: moduli (53,59) = 3127 cells: -1.95/-2.00/-2.05 pt at a 15% budget and -0.65/-0.75/-0.90 pt at 25% against a flat k-means of k=2858 at the same row budget; every CI entirely below 0. Coarser moduli are far worse (-7.3 to -8.4 pt at 15%).
ranked_verdict.memory_effect: 0.769 MB of auxiliary structure against 9.374 MB for the flat partition, a 12.2x reduction -- of which the centroid table alone goes from 8.78 MB to 0.172 MB (51x). But the whole 9.374 MB is 4.3% of the 219 MB fp32 arena that actually drives peak RSS, so saving 8.6 MB buys 3.9% of the wrong number.
ranked_verdict.honest_note_on_the_CRT_itself: the CRT is a labelling device. It lets a composite cell id be inverted back into its J residues with arithmetic instead of a table, and it is genuinely the right tool for that. It does not change the partition: the partition is the product of the J sub-quantisers, and that product is what loses the 1-2 pt.

ranked_verdict.arm: (d1) CRT over the document id alone -- no stored assignment map
ranked_verdict.finding: 13.60% recall@4 at a 15% budget and 21.15% at 25%, against 76.90 and 77.05 for the flat k-means partition (deltas -63.30 and -55.90 pt). Both figures are indistinguishable from scanning a random 15% or 25% of the corpus, which is exactly what a content-blind partition is.
ranked_verdict.why_it_was_still_worth_running: it is the literal reading of 'compute a document's cell from its id with no stored assignment map', and it makes the real point: after compact(recluster=True) nanomem ALREADY derives a document's cell from its id with no stored map, because cell = row // cell_target on a cell-ordered file. The map-free property costs nothing and is already there; arithmetic on the id cannot add information the layout does not already carry.

verdict_ranked.what_i_would_ship: Nothing as a default. The PCA-256 certified screen is the one mechanism here that works, and it is NOT a pre-registered win -- put it behind a flag and re-measure at the engine level before any default changes. Do not ship power-mean pooling at any p, any low-discrepancy seeding, tropical cell scoring, or CRT sharding.
verdict_ranked.dropped_arms: none. All five menu items (a)-(e) were implemented and measured.
verdict_ranked.multiplicity_note: This study ran roughly 300 arm/budget/seed cells against a baseline. At 95% confidence that alone produces a handful of spurious 'CI lower bound > 0' rows, and phaseB contains 3 of them. No arm is called a win on a single cell; the only arm called a win is exact by proof and does not rest on a confidence interval at all.
verdict_ranked.quarantine_statement: This study did not read, load, score, tune on, or diagnose against scratch/refound/clean_chat_benchmark_persona4.json or scratch/refound/clean_chat_benchmark_heldout.json. No chat or persona corpus was used by any arm; every corpus is a HotpotQA paragraph embedding matrix. Neither quarantined file appears anywhere in exotic_routing.py or in any script this study ran.
verdict_ranked.settled_question_not_re-tested: No arm here applies a pointwise exponent to a single cosine. That question is closed by prime_routing_results.json :: kernel_autopsy (0 of 142,800 argsort positions differ for S13; antisymmetry error 0.0 at p = 12, 12.5, 13, 15). Every arm above either aggregates across elements or combines two or more variables.

verdict_ranked.baseline_latency_caveat: The 1.4700 ms 'exact' arm in phaseC_latency is the ARENA-LEVEL fp32 matvec A @ q at 71,433 x 768, not the engine-level p50 of 1.774 ms the orchestrator measured for the shipped build. It excludes engine overhead on purpose so that the 1.529x ratio is a ratio between two search kernels and nothing else. Any end-to-end claim has to be re-measured inside VaultEngine, which is exactly where the shipped router's arena-level promise turned into an engine-level regression (DECISIONS #3, engine_latency_replicates).

amendment_2026_09_16_verifier.why: A verifier found that this study's single claimed WIN does not satisfy its own binding pre-registered decision rule. The finding is accepted in full; nothing is re-measured, only re-labelled.

reclassification.why_arm_c_cannot_clear_it: An exactness-preserving screen returns the same top-4 as the exact scan, so its recall delta is identically 0 and its paired-bootstrap CI is [0.00, 0.00]. 'CI lower bound > 0' is unreachable by construction, not merely unmet.
what_the_arm_does_satisfy: exactness_arms: 0 bound violations in 14,286,600 document checks, 0 of 1000 queries with a differing top-4 SCORE vector, and a deterministic per-document certificate rather than an empirical count (certificate_audit).
latency_arms_extra_condition: measured p50 1.529x over B1 on the same box in interleaved replicates (phaseC_latency).
reclassification.why_that_is_not_enough: latency_arms_extra_condition is worded as an EXTRA condition on an arm sold on latency -- 'must ALSO show' -- not as a substitute bar. No alternative win criterion was pre-registered for an exactness-preserving mechanism. So the honest count under the rule as written is ZERO WINS, EIGHT NEGATIVES, with arm (c) reported as a real mechanism that the pre-registration has no category for.
reclassification.headline_after: ZERO WINS UNDER THE RULE AS WRITTEN. Eight negatives, plus one uncategorised mechanism that is exact by proof and 1.529x faster at the arena level.
reclassification.what_did_NOT_change: No measurement. The energy capture, survivor fractions, certificate audit, latency table and every negative arm stand exactly as recorded; an independent reimplementation by the verifier got 0.9337 captured energy against 0.9335, 199/200 exact top-4 ID sets with the remaining one a tie, and 1.458x against the 1.529x here.
reclassification.rule_defect_for_next_time: A decision rule scored on a recall delta cannot classify a mechanism whose recall delta is zero by design. A future pre-registration needs a third category -- EXACT AND CHEAPER: zero differing top-k score vectors, a deterministic certificate, and a CI on the LATENCY ratio whose upper bound is < 1.0 -- declared before measurement, not after.

preregistration_provenance.finding_accepted: The claim that the pre-registration was written before any measurement cannot be independently verified for this study. exotic_routing.py is untracked by git, contains no code that writes the preregistration key, and no phase recorded its own completion time.
preregistration_provenance.what_supports_it: save() merges each phase into the existing JSON preserving key order, and 'preregistration' is the first of twelve keys; had it been added after phase0 it would sort last.
preregistration_provenance.what_cuts_against_it: phase_cert_audit and phase_rss_implication are defined BELOW the __main__ guard, i.e. appended to the source after runs had begun -- though the certificate they produce was itself required by the pre-registered exactness_arms clause.
preregistration_provenance.fix_applied: save() now stamps every phase with _saved_utc, so from the next run onward the ordering is readable off the file: every phase stamp must be later than preregistration.written_utc. Sections already in this file carry no stamp and their ordering remains self-reported.
